orgAdmin.title: Admin console
orgAdmin.notAdmin: Only owners and admins of this organization can open its admin console.
orgAdmin.overview.description: How your organization is doing, and what needs your attention.
orgAdmin.overview.membersHint: {invited, plural, =0 {No open invitations} one {# open invitation} other {# open invitations}} · {waiting, plural, =0 {none waiting} other {# waiting}}
orgAdmin.overview.vaultsHint: {pending, plural, =0 {All keys up to date} one {# waits for a new key} other {# wait for a new key}}
orgAdmin.overview.waiting: {count, plural, one {# person waits} other {# people wait}} for you to confirm them.
orgAdmin.overview.recoveryRequests: {count, plural, one {# member asks} other {# members ask}} to recover their account.
orgAdmin.overview.rotation: {count, plural, one {# vault waits} other {# vaults wait}} for a new key after someone left.
orgAdmin.overview.chainBroken: The activity log does not verify from entry #{seq} on. Someone may have changed or deleted entries.
orgAdmin.overview.resign: The policy was signed by someone who is no longer an admin. Sign it again so new devices accept it.
orgAdmin.overview.withoutTwoFactor: {count, plural, one {# member has} other {# members have}} not turned on two-factor sign-in, which your policy requires.
orgAdmin.overview.noPolicy: There is no policy yet. Set rules such as two-factor sign-in or a maximum auto-lock time.
orgAdmin.overview.noRecovery: Recovery through the organization is not set up. Members who forget their master password cannot get back in.
orgAdmin.overview.unused: {count, plural, one {# vault was} other {# vaults were}} not used in the last {days} days.
orgAdmin.members.description: Invite people, confirm them, change roles, pause access and offboard members who leave.
orgAdmin.offboard.title: Offboard {name}
orgAdmin.offboard.text: {name} loses access to this organization at once. Every vault key {name} had is replaced, so new and changed items stay out of reach.
orgAdmin.offboard.noAccess: {name} has no vaults in this organization.
orgAdmin.offboard.handoverText: {name} is the only manager of these vaults. Choose who manages them from now on; otherwise their members keep access, but only admins who are members can change who has access.
orgAdmin.offboard.cannotHandOver: You have no access to this vault, so you cannot hand it over. Ask {name} to share it with a successor before you offboard them.
orgAdmin.offboard.endSessionsHint: Also ends access to their personal vaults until they sign in again. Nothing is deleted.
orgAdmin.offboard.consequence: What {name} has already seen, they may have kept. Change the passwords they had access to.
orgAdmin.offboard.doneText: {name} no longer has access. The vault keys this device manages were replaced.
orgAdmin.offboard.pending: {count, plural, one {# vault waits} other {# vaults wait}} for its manager to replace the key:
orgAdmin.vaults.description: Shared vaults of the organization, who can open them and how they are used.
orgAdmin.vaults.accessText: People with access, directly or through a group, and their role.
orgAdmin.vaults.zeroKnowledge: Vault names and items are encrypted. You see the names of vaults you are a member of; the server only knows IDs, members and dates.
orgAdmin.access.legend: V view, E edit, M manage. * means access through a group.
orgAdmin.groups.description: Share a vault once with a group instead of with every person.
orgAdmin.policy.description: Rules for every member's apps. You sign each version with your key, so the server cannot loosen them.
orgAdmin.policy.none: No policy yet. Members' apps use their own settings.
orgAdmin.policy.needsResign: The person who signed this policy is no longer an admin. Devices keep the rules they already had, but new devices cannot verify them. Sign the policy again.
orgAdmin.policy.unknownRules: This app does not know these rules yet: {rules}. Update Passbox to enforce them.
orgAdmin.policy.historyText: Every version, newest first, checked on this device.
orgAdmin.policy.historyUnverifiedHint: The signer is no longer an admin, so this device cannot check this older version.
orgAdmin.policy.requireTwoFactorHint: Members are asked to turn it on and cannot turn it off.
orgAdmin.policy.minScoreHint: Checked on the member's device when they unlock. Passbox never sees master passwords.
orgAdmin.policy.autoLockHint: Members can choose a shorter time, not a longer one.
orgAdmin.policy.forbidExportHint: Items of the organization's vaults cannot be exported.
orgAdmin.policy.forbidExternalSharingHin: Items of the organization's vaults cannot be moved or copied to personal vaults or other organizations.
orgAdmin.policy.allowPersonalVaultHint: When off, members cannot create personal vaults or new items in them. Existing items stay readable.
orgAdmin.policy.shareLinksHint: Links that share a snapshot of an item with people outside Passbox.
orgAdmin.policy.requireRecoveryHint: Members are asked to let the organization recover their account.
orgAdmin.policy.requireRecoveryNotSetUp: Set up recovery in the Recovery section first; until then members cannot enroll.
orgAdmin.policy.reportUsageHint: Members' apps log when someone views, reveals, copies or fills an item of the organization's vaults. Signed by their app, without contents. Members see that this is on.
orgAdmin.policy.reviewText: These rules apply to every member as soon as their apps sync. You sign them with your account key.
orgAdmin.policy.howText: Each version is signed by an owner or admin and checked by every member's app against the organization's verified members. A server can neither change the rules nor bring back an older, looser version on devices that saw the newer one.
orgAdmin.policy.howLimits: The apps enforce the rules; the server additionally refuses turning two-factor sign-in off and new personal vaults. A modified app can ignore a policy, and a server can withhold a new version from devices that have not seen it yet.
orgAdmin.rule.minScore.on: Master passwords must be at least “{level}”.
orgAdmin.rule.autoLock.on: Apps lock after at most {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without activity.
orgAdmin.rule.autoLock.off: No limit for the auto-lock time.
orgAdmin.rule.export.on: Items of the organization cannot be exported.
orgAdmin.rule.external.on: Items stay in the organization's vaults.
orgAdmin.rule.external.off: Items can be moved to other vaults.
orgAdmin.rule.links.restricted: Share links last at most {days} days.
orgAdmin.rule.links.restrictedViews: Share links last at most {days} days and open at most {views} times.
orgAdmin.rule.recovery.on: Members must enroll in recovery through the organization.
orgAdmin.rule.usage.on: Viewing, revealing, copying and filling items is logged.
orgAdmin.summary.title: Policy
orgAdmin.summary.text: Rules your organization set for everyone (version {version}, signed by an admin).
orgAdmin.summary.none: The policy does not restrict anything.
orgAdmin.banner.two_factor.title: {orgs} requires two-factor sign-in
orgAdmin.banner.two_factor.body: Turn it on to keep access.
orgAdmin.banner.password_strength.title: Your organization requires a stronger master password
orgAdmin.banner.password_strength.body: Choose a longer one, for example four random words.
orgAdmin.banner.recovery_enrollment.titl: {orgs} asks you to enroll in recovery
orgAdmin.banner.recovery_enrollment.body: Then an admin can help you if you forget your master password.
orgAdmin.banner.update_app.title: Your organization's policy has rules this app does not know
orgAdmin.banner.enrolled: You are enrolled in recovery through your organization.
orgAdmin.audit.description: What happened in your organization. Entries are hash-chained, so later changes and deletions are visible.
orgAdmin.audit.chainValidServer: The server checked all {count} entries: the chain is intact.
orgAdmin.audit.chainValidHere: This device checked all {count} entries: the chain is intact.
orgAdmin.audit.chainBrokenLong: The chain is broken at entry #{seq}: an entry was changed or deleted.
orgAdmin.audit.chainHint: Whoever controls the database could rewrite everything after a point. Export the log or connect a SIEM to keep an independent copy.
orgAdmin.audit.exportFailed: The activity log could not be exported
orgAdmin.audit.exportBroken: Careful: the exported chain does not verify from entry #{seq} on.
orgAdmin.audit.action.member_role_change: Changed the role of {target} from {from} to {to}
orgAdmin.audit.action.member_reattested: Vouched again for the key of {target}
orgAdmin.audit.action.group_member_added: Added a member to the group {target}
orgAdmin.audit.action.group_key_rotated: Replaced the key of the group {target}
orgAdmin.audit.action.vault_access_revok: Removed access to {target} and replaced its key
orgAdmin.audit.action.vault_items_writte: Re-encrypted {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} in {target}
orgAdmin.audit.action.recovery_key_creat: Set up recovery through the organization
orgAdmin.audit.action.recovery_completed: Recovered their account and chose a new master password
orgAdmin.audit.action.member_recovery_co: Signed in with a two-factor recovery code
orgAdmin.reports.description: Security and access across your organization. Members' apps report numbers only, never items or passwords.
orgAdmin.reports.securityHint: The score covers the logins a member can see in their personal vaults and this organization's vaults: weak, reused and unsecured passwords lower it.
orgAdmin.reports.privacy: Apps report once a day after unlocking. Reports contain counts and a score only.
orgAdmin.reports.unusedHint: Vaults without changes or logged use in the last {days} days. Usage is only known when the policy logs item usage.
orgAdmin.recovery.description: Let admins help members who forget their master password, without seeing vault contents.
orgAdmin.recovery.required: Your policy requires every member to enroll.
orgAdmin.recovery.optional: Enrollment is optional. You can require it in the policy.
orgAdmin.recovery.honest: An admin who approves a recovery briefly holds the member's account key on their device. Every recovery is logged and the member is notified.
orgAdmin.integrations.description: Send the activity log to your SIEM: let it fetch entries with a token, or push new entries to a webhook.
orgAdmin.integrations.tokensText: A token lets a collector read this organization's activity log, and nothing else.
orgAdmin.integrations.tokenNameHint: For example the system that uses it: Splunk, Sentinel, Elastic.
orgAdmin.integrations.tokenOnce: It is shown only once. Store it in your SIEM's secret store.
orgAdmin.integrations.revokeText: Collectors using it stop receiving entries at once.
orgAdmin.integrations.pullHint: Fetch entries in order and pass the last sequence number as “after”:
orgAdmin.integrations.webhooksText: New entries are sent in batches to an HTTPS address, signed with a secret.
orgAdmin.integrations.urlHint: HTTPS, reachable from the Passbox server.
orgAdmin.integrations.fromStartHint: Otherwise only entries from now on are sent.
orgAdmin.integrations.secretOnce: It is shown only once. Use it to check the X-Passbox-Signature header of each delivery.
orgAdmin.integrations.failing: {count, plural, one {# failed attempt} other {# failed attempts}}
orgAdmin.integrations.pushHint: Deliveries are retried with increasing waits until your system answers with 2xx.
orgAdmin.integrations.docs: Guides for Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel and Elastic are in the documentation (docs/architecture/administration.md).
orgAdmin.settings.description: Name, how long the activity log is kept, and leaving or deleting the organization.
orgAdmin.settings.retentionText: Older entries are deleted automatically. The rest of the chain stays verifiable.
orgAdmin.settings.retentionWarning: Entries older than {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} are deleted for good. Export or connect a SIEM first if you need them longer.
orgAdmin.settings.autoLockLimited: Your organization allows at most {minutes} minutes.
orgAdmin.export.blocked: {count, plural, one {# vault is} other {# vaults are}} left out: your organization does not allow exporting them.
orgAdmin.error.personalVault: Your organization does not allow personal vaults. Save items in one of its shared vaults.
orgAdmin.error.twoFactorRequired: Your organization requires two-factor sign-in, so you cannot turn it off.
orgAdmin.error.policy: Your organization's policy does not allow this.
orgAdmin.integrations.worksWith: Works with any SIEM that can poll an HTTP API or receive webhooks, for example:
